source: Hoque, Ismamul - MSc Thesis (paper/Ismamul Hoque Msc Thesis.pdf), Table 4.1 mode choice component (12-alternative MNL, bicycle reference, 927 observations, GAUSS MAXLIK). Thesis ASCs: Bicycle(ref)=0.00, Bus=1.28***, MRT=1.37***, CNG=3.31***, Office Vehicle=1.20**, Ride-share Bike=-0.03(ns), Ride-share Car=4.60***, Rickshaw=2.27***, Lagoona=-0.502(ns), Private Motorcycle=1.87***, Private Car=3.09***, Walk=0.87*. beta_duration/beta_fare are pooled across all 12 alternatives in the thesis, not mode-specific. Units confirmed (not assumed) via the thesis's own stated VTTS: (0.112/0.034)*60 = 197.6 BDT/hr matches the thesis's reported ~200 BDT/hr only if duration is in MINUTES and fare is in raw BDT (not thousands).

mode_mapping.note: The thesis has 12 alternatives; this scenario simulates 7 modes. Where one of our modes is a COMPOSITE of several thesis alternatives, its ASC is the share-weighted average of the constituent thesis ASCs, weighted by that group's actual raw DTCA HTS trip counts (see 'composition' fields below) - NOT simply one constituent's ASC. Ratios are from the raw survey (raw_data/Dhaka/hts/dtca_full.xlsx, sheet 'trip info', column q61_trip_mode). Still not simulated separately: MRT (our transit schedule has no metro line at all - every one of its 154 lines is transportMode=bus, so there is nothing to route MRT on; also only 154 raw MRT trips, survey ran just after the first line opened), Train/Boat/Water Taxi/Ferry (folded into pt, ~1.4% of the pt bucket, not in the thesis either), Truck/Pickup (folded into car, 309 trips, not in the thesis either).
mode_mapping.paratransit: CNG auto-rickshaw - clean 1:1 with thesis (our bucket is exactly the 3-wheeler Auto/CNG shared+reserved variants)
mode_mapping.car: COMPOSITE: Private Car + Ride-share Car + Office Vehicle (+ Truck/Pickup, not in thesis)
mode_mapping.pt: COMPOSITE: Bus + Lagoona + MRT + school/staff buses (+ train/boat/water taxi, not in thesis)

composition.note: Raw DTCA HTS trip counts behind each composite bucket's share-weighted ASC, for auditability. Trips whose thesis alternative does not exist (Truck/Pickup, train/boat/water taxi) are excluded from the weighting but still simulated in that bucket.

motorcycle.rationale: All motorcycle variants are grouped because on the network they are physically the same vehicle (speed, fuel cost, filtering behaviour). The thesis's much lower ride-share bike ASC is carried through the share weighting rather than by simulating it separately.

pt.rationale: KNOWN RESIDUAL BIAS, deliberately left as-is for now: pt keeps Bus's ASC (1.28) rather than the share-weighted 1.023, overstating pt by ~0.26 utils (~2.3 min of travel time at beta_duration). The bucket is 79% bus so this is far milder than the car/motorcycle problem was (which was ~0.96 utils / 8.6 min). The cleaner fix is splitting Lagoona/Tempu out as its own road-based teleported mode - it is a human-hauler that is not in the GTFS at all and is currently being routed on bus transit lines it does not actually run on.

travel_time_model.note: Door-to-door travel-time proxy per mode: time_min = overhead_min + min_per_km * straight-line km. Used ONLY on the Python side - the synthesis-time seed assignment and dhaka/mode_choice/precalibrate_asc.py, which have no routing; the Java estimator uses real routed times. Fitted by OLS of total simulated trip time (every leg: access/egress walks, waiting, transfers) on euclidean_distance per main_mode, from simulation_output/ITERS/it.0/0.trips.csv.gz of the 2026-09-18 run (road modes on the network, ownership, fares on straight-line distance), top 1% of times trimmed. Replaces fallback_speed_kmh, a single constant speed per mode, which could not represent fixed overhead: door-to-door car speed runs from 6.6 km/h under 1 km to 18.7 over 10 km, pt from 3.1 to 11.5, but rickshaw only 4.2 to 6.5. Most trips are short (median 1.9 km), so a constant speed made car/pt/motorcycle about twice as fast as reality on short trips while barely flattering rickshaw - offline, car and pt looked competitive on short trips that the simulation then handed to rickshaw (rickshaw 30.1% -> 40.9% in one iteration). Interpretation: road modes carry ~5 min fixed overhead, pt ~17 min (walk to stop + wait). walk fits exactly (0 overhead, 19.7 min/km = 3.05 km/h = 1.1 m/s / 1.3) because it is teleported. R^2: rickshaw 0.76, bike 0.72, paratransit 0.51, motorcycle 0.48, pt 0.47, car 0.39 - the remainder is genuine route/congestion variation. Re-fit after any change that alters congestion or routing.

car.source: EFFECTIVE rate on this model's distance scale, calibrated to the DTCA survey's reported trip costs - NOT a real Dhaka tariff and NOT fuel cost. Replaces a fuel-only construction (122 BDT/l / 12 km/l = 10.2 BDT/km) that understated observed cost 5.1x, because this bucket is substantially ride-hailing plus, for private cars, a hired driver/parking/maintenance that respondents count as trip cost. Re-run calibrate_fares.py if the distance construction changes.

motorcycle.source: EFFECTIVE rate on this model's distance scale, calibrated to reported costs - NOT fuel cost. The old 122 BDT/l / 35 km/l = 3.5 BDT/km understated observed cost 3.6x; the bucket includes Pathao/Uber ride-share bike fares.

pt.source: Minimum fare + per-km, the real BRTA bus structure, but the per-km rate is an EFFECTIVE rate on this model's distance scale calibrated to reported costs (the regulated ~2.5 BDT/km with a 10 BDT minimum predicted 10 BDT against 20 observed).

paratransit.source: Re-levelled for SHARED (per-seat) CNG, which is what most of this bucket is, NOT the official BRTA reserved meter rate of 40 BDT for the first 2 km plus 12 BDT/km. That reserved rate overstated observed cost 3.9x - and at 12 BDT/km the structure exceeds the observed median before any flag fall, so it cannot be kept. EFFECTIVE rates on this model's distance scale.

rickshaw.source: EFFECTIVE rate on this model's distance scale, calibrated to reported costs. Supersedes the previous UNVERIFIED PLACEHOLDER of 10 BDT/km - which the data shows was close (13.4 predicted vs 20 observed), the smallest error of any mode.

walk.source: Zero-fare (thesis, and 94.4% of survey walk trips report zero cost).

bike.source: Zero-fare (thesis, and 94.9% of survey bike trips report zero cost).

fare_assumptions.note: Calibrated by dhaka/mode_choice/calibrate_fares.py against the DTCA survey's reported trip costs (q55_total_cost). Only the LEVEL of each fare function is data-estimated; the SHAPE is retained from external tariff sources because ward-sampled distance is too noisy to identify a slope (66.3% of survey trips are intra-ward, giving an almost flat observed cost-vs-distance profile that is an artifact, not behaviour). Every rate here is an EFFECTIVE rate on this model's ward-sampled distance scale - valid because the survey and the synthetic population share that scale, but NOT a real Dhaka tariff. Re-run the script if the distance construction ever changes.

asc_provenance: Pre-calibrated offline by dhaka/mode_choice/precalibrate_asc.py against the mode_hts_donor target shares, starting from the thesis's published ASCs (which are kept verbatim in this file's 'source' and 'composition' fields). The values in 'asc' are therefore NO LONGER the thesis values - see 'source' for those. They are still to be refined by MATSim calibration rounds via dhaka/mode_choice/calibrate_asc.py, which corrects the part of the gap only the simulation can reveal: congested car time, routed pt time, tour-level choice, and congestion feedback.

income_scaling.formula: beta_fare(person) = beta_fare_per_bdt * (income_bdt / reference_income_bdt) ** (-elasticity); persons with unknown income (class -1 or missing) get beta_fare_per_bdt unscaled
income_scaling.source: Hoque's model has a single pooled beta_fare, which implies one VTTS of 197.6 BDT/h for everyone. Against implied wages from the DTCA income brackets that is 4.22x the wage for the Tk 10-20k bracket but 0.49x for >Tk 100k, where conventional VTTS is 0.3-0.5x the wage - the signature of a model estimated on affluent residence-choice respondents and applied to a poorer all-trip population. Scaling cost sensitivity with income is standard practice (eqasim's utility functions do the same). With beta_duration fixed, VTTS scales as income**elasticity. elasticity=0.5 is the cross-sectional income elasticity of VTTS typically found in meta-analyses (Abrantes & Wardman 2011; Wardman, Chintakayala & de Jong 2016) - a LITERATURE value, not estimated here. reference_income is the DTCA trip-weighted median household income (bracket Tk 50-60k, cumulative 46.8% -> 58.0%), so beta_fare is exactly Hoque's value for the median household and the transfer is preserved at the centre of the distribution. class_midpoints are bracket midpoints; the open top bracket (>Tk 100k) is set to 130k, an ASSUMPTION. What this does NOT fix: the average VTTS level stays Hoque's; it redistributes it. With elasticity 0.5 the VTTS/wage spread narrows from 0.49x-4.22x to roughly 0.75x-2.20x, so low-income travellers are still valued above their wage.

ownership_constants.source: Vehicle ownership, modelled as a UTILITY PENALTY for persons whose household owns none of that vehicle type (non_owner_constant is added to that mode's utility), not as a hard availability gate. Evidence from the DTCA survey (q15_vehicles per member), on the SAME basis the population is synthesised from - study-area households, expansion-weighted: 11.1% of households own a car, 20.6% a motorcycle, 2.1% a bicycle (the synthetic population reproduces this: 10.9 / 20.5 / 2.2%). Car-owning households are under-sampled and heavily up-weighted, so the unweighted all-survey figures (2.7 / 9.2 / 2.5%) are NOT comparable. Owning households make 85.5% of car, 90.7% of motorcycle and 79.0% of bike trips, so ownership dominates but is NOT absolute - non-owners still make 14.5% / 9.3% / 21.0% of those trips, through staff and company cars, ride-hailing (Uber/Pathao), chauffeured or family vehicles, and borrowed bikes. A hard gate would delete those trips; the penalty keeps them possible and is calibrated so the non-owner share of each mode's trips reproduces target_non_owner_trip_share (dhaka/mode_choice/precalibrate_asc.py fits it jointly with the ASCs). This REPLACES DiscreteModeChoice's built-in 'Car' mode availability, which gated car on a driving licence: only 4.9% of persons hold one, yet 60.3% of survey car trips are made by people without a licence (82% of those 'drive by driver' - chauffeured). That gate made most real car use impossible and is the likely main cause of car collapsing from 7.2% to ~2.7% in the September runs. It also read an attribute named 'carAvail', so the population's 'carAvailability' was never consulted at all.
